newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe women petition state on female condom.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe women petition state on female condom.

text.p: A leading Zimbabwean group fighting against the spread of the HIV virus which causes AIDS on Sunday petitioned the government to make the female condom freely and cheaply available to help the country battle the pandemic.

Women and AIDS Support Network (WASN) spokesman Priscilla Misihairabwi said the focus on the male condom as one of the main means of preventing HIV infection had failed to stem the pandemic because the majority of men refused to use it, particularly with their wives.
WASN is a non-government organisation which co-ordinates anti-AIDS campaigns.

"Surveys done here (in Zimbabwe) show that both men and women prefer the female condom to the male one so we are petitioning the government to make it freely available and affordable," Misihairabwi told Reuters.

The condom -- which consists of a loose-fitting polyurethane sheath joined by two flexible rings -- is not yet available on the local market and Misihairabwi said preliminary research had shown that it would be too expensive for the ordinary Zimbabwean woman.

"Like in other African countries, Zimbabwean women generally have no control on their sexual lives and studies here have indicated that for most women in monogamous relationships, the risk from their partners is very high because male promiscuity is no issue," she said.
"So the female condom is an important initiative to get women to have control over their sexual destinies and protect themselves from infection," she added.
The petition was presented to the Deputy Speaker of Parliament, Edna Madzongwe, at a concert by some of the country's top musicians held to mark World AIDS Day.
Zimbabwe is one of the African countries hardest hit by the AIDS pandemic, with an estimated 10 percent of its 10.5 million population HIV-infected.
